data.name: Aztez
data.detailed_description:
Brutally satisfying beat-em-up combat, set in the Aztec empire. Choose your fights in a turn-based metagame.

Aztez is a unique hybrid of beat 'em up and turn-based strategy set in the world of the Aztec Empire. Deploy your Aztez (elite close combat warriors) in the metagame and enjoy a highly technical real-time combat event that has consequences in the empire. But choose your missions wisely, as you have limited deployments! A great enemy approaches the Valley Of Mexico, and it will require all of your skill and cunning to take them on and change the course of history...



  • Highly replayable Campaign game that changes every play-through. Different events, artifacts, and battles every game.
  • Experience huge Empire cities, stunning natural vistas, and even the Aztec underworld!
  • Perform sacrifices, score enormous combos, and summon immensely powerful Aztec gods.
  • Fight against historical warriors and mythological foes alike using 8 distinct weapons.
  • Find and equip over 70 cosmetic items.
  • Or enjoy a purified combat experience in the great capital city arena!

data.short_description: Aztez is a highly stylized, brutally satisfying beat 'em up set in the world of the Aztec Empire. Take on the role of an elite close combat unit and undergo missions on behalf of the Empire in the turn-based metagame, and fight against warriors and mythological foes alike using 8 unique weapons in real time combat mode.

reviews.review:
Aztez is an unusual blend of brutal beat ’em up action and light turn-based strategy that manages to feel different from most games in either genre. Developed and published by Team Colorblind, it places players within a heavily stylized interpretation of the Aztec Empire, where elite warriors are deployed to resolve conflicts across a changing strategic map. Instead of presenting combat as a simple sequence of disconnected stages, the campaign gives each confrontation a larger purpose, creating an experience that mixes strategic decision-making with demanding real-time fighting.

Combat is easily the strongest part of the experience. The fighting system encourages far more than repeatedly attacking whatever enemy happens to be nearby. Players can create lengthy combinations, launch opponents, evade incoming attacks, control groups of enemies, and use different techniques depending on the weapon currently equipped. There are eight weapons available, and their differences provide enough flexibility for players to develop preferred approaches while still rewarding experimentation. Learning how attacks connect into one another becomes increasingly important as enemies grow more dangerous.

The fighting also benefits from a wonderfully exaggerated sense of violence and spectacle. Sacrifices and supernatural powers inspired by Aztec mythology give encounters additional personality, while mythological creatures appear alongside more conventional warriors. Battles can become chaotic, particularly when several opponents attack simultaneously, but mastering that chaos is part of the appeal. Successful encounters eventually feel less like frantic button pressing and more like carefully controlled performances in which positioning, timing, weapon knowledge, and combo execution all matter.

Its visual presentation makes an equally strong impression. The predominantly monochromatic environments and characters are contrasted by vivid splashes of red, giving the action an immediately recognizable appearance. This minimalist approach is more than an artistic gimmick because it complements the violent combat exceptionally well. Blood, movement, and attacks stand out clearly against the restrained backgrounds. Locations range from imperial settlements and wilderness areas to supernatural environments, allowing the game to explore both historical inspiration and mythology without being constrained by realism.

Outside combat, the campaign shifts into a turn-based strategic structure. Players oversee events throughout the empire and must determine where their limited Aztez warriors should be deployed. Because not every situation can necessarily receive equal attention, decisions carry consequences. The campaign incorporates randomized events, battles, and artifacts, meaning subsequent attempts can develop differently. This provides a welcome roguelike quality and makes failure easier to accept because restarting can produce new circumstances rather than simply forcing players through an identical campaign again.

The strategy component is interesting, although it is noticeably less sophisticated than the fighting system. Players expecting a deep historical grand-strategy simulation will probably find it comparatively lightweight. Its primary purpose is to connect battles, create uncertainty, and force the player to consider when intervention is worthwhile. That approach works well enough, but there are moments when the strategic management feels like connective tissue between the much more exciting combat encounters. Fortunately, players primarily interested in fighting can also make use of the arena to practice and enjoy the combat mechanics more directly.

Replay value is strengthened by the unpredictable campaign structure, combat mastery, different weapons, artifacts, and a substantial collection of cosmetic items. More than seventy cosmetic pieces provide additional customization and collectible incentives. These additions do not dramatically alter the fundamentals of combat, but they contribute to the sense of progression. Steam achievements, leaderboards, cloud support, full controller support, and Family Sharing further complement the package. Controller play is especially appropriate because the fast fighting and combination-focused mechanics feel naturally suited to a gamepad.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently listed as Unknown rather than officially Verified, Playable, or Unsupported. The game does have a native Linux version and full controller support, which are encouraging characteristics for handheld use, but these should not be mistaken for an official Deck compatibility rating. Players purchasing specifically for Steam Deck should therefore consider its official compatibility status unverified and be prepared for possible configuration or compatibility issues.

Aztez ultimately succeeds because of how confidently it commits to its central combat system. The strategic layer is not equally deep, and the campaign structure can sometimes feel secondary to the fighting, but it gives the action meaningful context and helps distinguish the game from conventional arcade brawlers. The combination of responsive combat, eight weapons, mythological elements, procedural campaign variation, memorable art direction, and an unusually underused historical setting creates something with a strong personality. It is particularly rewarding for players who enjoy mastering combos and improving their mechanical performance rather than simply progressing through a story once.

Rating: 8/10
